additional_info.subject: Note from end customer
additional_info.body:
Our Volvo truck tried different outlets in the morning.
Although it was alone at the charging station, only 60–70 kW were delivered.
At dispenser outlet 3, with around 79 kW, the highest power was achieved.
Then an Iveco arrived.
Neither outlet 1 nor 2 allowed activation or connection.
Never seen before: the four circles on the display were not running in sync.
See video.
Restarted the charging station via the display.

additional_info.subject: 0442829 - ID0442829-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP/R6 170002000] Outlet1/2 Issue CRM:00314000222
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr. Glöckner,
I am reaching out from the Expert Services Team in regards of ticket
ID0442829
. Apologies for the delayed answer.
The ticket was opened to request an analysis of a test session performed on 08.08.2025 with Iveco and Volvo trucks, which resulted in several errors.
Here are the findings of my analysis:
1) At 2025-08-08T06:00:39, Volvo truck with EVMAC "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62
" was connected to DC3. Charging started at 2025-08-08T06:01:11, and power provided was 80kW (MaxPower of primary converter group (CGp) for DC3). From the logs, I see the contactors of the matrix moving in order to allocate more power, but the session was ended at 2025-08-08T06:01:50.
2) At 2025-08-08T06:03:30. Volvo truck "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62
" is connected to DC1. At first, 60kW are provided to the outlet (MaxPower of CGp for DC1). From 2025-08-08T06:04:14, all 4 converter groups are allocated to DC1, but the power is not upscaling. At 2025-08-08T06:05:12 the session is stopped.
3) At 2025-08-08T06:06:50 Volvo truck "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62
" is connected to DC3. Power provided was 80kW (MaxPower of CGp for DC3). All 4 converter groups are allocated to DC1, but the power is not upscaling.
4)While Volvo truck is still charging at DC3, at 2025-08-08T06:34:33 Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" is connected to DC2. Session fails in Parameter discovery due to "code":54,"msg":"ERR_EVCOM, EV communication problem detected".
5) At 2025-08-08T06:38:06,
Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
is connected to DC2. Session fails during Cablecheck due to code":67,"msg":"ERR_EV_DROPPED, vehicle ended with unexpected pilot state B".
6) At 2025-08-08T06:41:11,
Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
is connected to DC1. Session fails during PreCharge due to code "code":67,"msg":"ERR_EV_DROPPED, vehicle ended with unexpected pilot state B".
7) DC3 is stopped and a reboot is launched.
8) After reboot, at 2025-08-08T07:01:10, a different Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.47.27
" is connected to DC1. Charging starts at 2025-08-08T07:01:42, providing 140kW to the EV (according EV demand). At 2025-08-08T07:02:44 the other Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" is connected to DC2 and starts charging. At 2025-08-08T07:03:43 DC1 is interrupted due to loss of Fbk from outgoing coil QA21-22:
9) The subsequent sessions at 2025-08-08T07:04:43, at 2025-08-08T07:06:51, at 2025-08-08T07:08:25 and at 2025-08-08T07:10:00, all on DC1, are all failing at CableCheck as QA21-22 is not providing feedback.
10) Reboot is launched.
11)After reboot, at 2025-08-08T07:22:52 the Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.47.27
" is connected to DC1. It starts charging initailly with 60kW (maxPower of CGp for DC1), and after few seconds available power is raised to 300kW.
12) At 2025-08-08T07:24:14 on DC3 is connected Volvo truck EVAMC "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62"
and starts charging at 80kW (power allocated according to FIFS logic).
13) DC1 is disconnected and DC3 goes up to 300kW. After this point I did not see any error anymore.
Comments:
Point 1:
I believe here not enough time was given to the charger to upscale the power.
Points 2, 3
:
from the logs, I do not see enough information to understand if the charger was limiting the power, or if the truck was request too few. At point 13, we see that the Volvo truck eventually asked for full power, but in that specific moment I cannot tell from where the limitation was coming from.
Suggestion:
By the end of this current week (CW34) we are releasing a new SichargeD FW
v8.0.5
, which includes important improvements and new features in terms of Dynamic Power Allocation, by basing the power delivery not on EVSOC and EVMAXPower anymore, but more independent from
EV.SOC levels and providing a more efficient utilization of charger installed capacity by allocating/de-allocating converter groups to DC outlets based on EV power demand.
My suggestion is to update the charger to
v8.0.5
, perform further tests and verify if this power limitation still happens.
Point 4,5,6
: Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" caused the session interruptions, by interrupting the communication (error54) or by suddenly dropping the pilot state from C to B (error 67). I would suggest to contact the manufacturer and have this particular vehicle checked.
Point 8 and 9
:
Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" was still used, and when the truck started the session, the other outlet was stopped. Given that few moments before the same truck was not able to start the charging, I wouldn't exclude that this truck caused the interruption of the first outlet.
After that, it seems that outlet 1 could not start due to QA21-22 not responding anymore. I am suspecting that, more than the QA21-22 not replying, was the EcoG or state monitor not commanding to close, as if stuck after the session interruption. Only a reboot restored the situation.
Questions:
Have you experienced other issues with this specific EV
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
?
Have you experienced other times a parallel disconnection between DC1 and DC2 (i.e. DC2 connecting and DC1 interrupting)? Or did it happen only with
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87?
I hope my analysis provided you with answers and clarity to the test session.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you to my questions, and to hear about the test sessions after v8.0.5 is installed.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
Smart Infrastructure

additional_info.body:
Hi Mr. Servidei,
We just want to understand a little bit Siemens’ algorithms. In the morning we had a strange issue:
1.
# 08h51 Outlet 1+2 were busy by Volvo and Iveco. They waited about 1 hour (!) … but only 59 + 80 kW power.
2.
# 08h59 Iveco on outlet 2 had to go on tour – we just changed just-for-fun to outlet 3.
è
in the meantime Volvo on outlet 1 stay frozen at 59 kW
è
09:01: same picture with low power 59 kW (outlet 1) and 80 kW (outlet 3)  …we could wait only some minutes … no change.
3.
# 09:09 Volvo on outlet 1 – the only truck – but still 59 kW
4.
# 09:10 an other Iveco started at outlet 4 … suddenly the was full power 216 kW (outlet 1 … first-come first-served) and 80 kW (outlet 4)  <- that’s perfect
5.
# 09:27 Volvo had to go -> full power to outlet 4 (272 kW) <- that’s ok, too.
-> 4+5 … ok
-> 2+3 … we can’t evaluate …perhaps a to short time for re assign converter  (we believe there would have been no change)
-> 1     ….
Not ok. There was a time when it worked well in version 7.0.5.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen

Wenn Ihnen der Absender nicht bekannt ist, dürfen Links und Anhänge nicht geklickt bzw. geöffnet werden. Bei verdächtigen Mails wenden Sie sich bitte umgehend an den IT-Support (DW -379).
Dear Mr. Glöckner,
I am reaching out from the Expert Services Team in regards of ticket
ID0442829
. Apologies for the delayed answer.
The ticket was opened to request an analysis of a test session performed on 08.08.2025 with Iveco and Volvo trucks, which resulted in several errors.
Here are the findings of my analysis:
1) At 2025-08-08T06:00:39, Volvo truck with EVMAC "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62
" was connected to DC3. Charging started at 2025-08-08T06:01:11, and power provided was 80kW (MaxPower of primary converter group (CGp) for DC3). From the logs, I see the contactors of the matrix moving in order to allocate more power, but the session was ended at 2025-08-08T06:01:50.
2) At 2025-08-08T06:03:30. Volvo truck "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62
" is connected to DC1. At first, 60kW are provided to the outlet (MaxPower of CGp for DC1). From 2025-08-08T06:04:14, all 4 converter groups are allocated to DC1, but the power is not upscaling. At 2025-08-08T06:05:12 the session is stopped.
3) At 2025-08-08T06:06:50 Volvo truck "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62
" is connected to DC3. Power provided was 80kW (MaxPower of CGp for DC3). All 4 converter groups are allocated to DC1, but the power is not upscaling.
4)While Volvo truck is still charging at DC3, at 2025-08-08T06:34:33 Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" is connected to DC2. Session fails in Parameter discovery due to "code":54,"msg":"ERR_EVCOM, EV communication problem detected".
5) At 2025-08-08T06:38:06,
Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
is connected to DC2. Session fails during Cablecheck due to code":67,"msg":"ERR_EV_DROPPED, vehicle ended with unexpected pilot state B".
6) At 2025-08-08T06:41:11,
Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
is connected to DC1. Session fails during PreCharge due to code "code":67,"msg":"ERR_EV_DROPPED, vehicle ended with unexpected pilot state B".
7) DC3 is stopped and a reboot is launched.
8) After reboot, at 2025-08-08T07:01:10, a different Iveco truck EVMAC "
5c.cc.a0.02.47.27
" is connected to DC1. Charging starts at 2025-08-08T07:01:42, providing 140kW to the EV (according EV demand). At 2025-08-08T07:02:44 the other Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" is connected to DC2 and starts charging. At 2025-08-08T07:03:43 DC1 is interrupted due to loss of Fbk from outgoing coil QA21-22:
9) The subsequent sessions at 2025-08-08T07:04:43, at 2025-08-08T07:06:51, at 2025-08-08T07:08:25 and at 2025-08-08T07:10:00, all on DC1, are all failing at CableCheck as QA21-22 is not providing feedback.
10) Reboot is launched.
11)After reboot, at 2025-08-08T07:22:52 the Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.47.27
" is connected to DC1. It starts charging initailly with 60kW (maxPower of CGp for DC1), and after few seconds available power is raised to 300kW.
12) At 2025-08-08T07:24:14 on DC3 is connected Volvo truck EVAMC "
00.16.81.0e.e6.62"
and starts charging at 80kW (power allocated according to FIFS logic).
13) DC1 is disconnected and DC3 goes up to 300kW. After this point I did not see any error anymore.
Comments:
Point 1:
I believe here not enough time was given to the charger to upscale the power.
Points 2, 3
:
from the logs, I do not see enough information to understand if the charger was limiting the power, or if the truck was request too few. At point 13, we see that the Volvo truck eventually asked for full power, but in that specific moment I cannot tell from where the limitation was coming from.
Suggestion:
By the end of this current week (CW34) we are releasing a new SichargeD FW
v8.0.5
, which includes important improvements and new features in terms of Dynamic Power Allocation, by basing the power delivery not on EVSOC and EVMAXPower anymore, but more independent from
EV.SOC levels and providing a more efficient utilization of charger installed capacity by allocating/de-allocating converter groups to DC outlets based on EV power demand.
My suggestion is to update the charger to
v8.0.5
, perform further tests and verify if this power limitation still happens.
Point 4,5,6
: Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" caused the session interruptions, by interrupting the communication (error54) or by suddenly dropping the pilot state from C to B (error 67). I would suggest to contact the manufacturer and have this particular vehicle checked.
Point 8 and 9
:
Iveco truck "
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
" was still used, and when the truck started the session, the other outlet was stopped. Given that few moments before the same truck was not able to start the charging, I wouldn't exclude that this truck caused the interruption of the first outlet.
After that, it seems that outlet 1 could not start due to QA21-22 not responding anymore. I am suspecting that, more than the QA21-22 not replying, was the EcoG or state monitor not commanding to close, as if stuck after the session interruption. Only a reboot restored the situation.
Questions:
1.
Have you experienced other issues with this specific EV
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87
?
2.
Have you experienced other times a parallel disconnection between DC1 and DC2 (i.e. DC2 connecting and DC1 interrupting)? Or did it happen only with
5c.cc.a0.02.62.87?
I hope my analysis provided you with answers and clarity to the test session.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you to my questions, and to hear about the test sessions after v8.0.5 is installed.
With kind regards,
